To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the threshold current density, the temperature parameter, the differential efficiency, and the watt-ampere characteristics are sensitive to the anisotropic deformation that is caused by the mismatch of lattice periods.

(1) the threshold current density and differential efficiency of the laser diodes can pass through a minimum as the lattice mismatch is increased; (2) the radiative characteristics depend on the sign of the strain; and (3) the radiative parameters are more sensitive to the lattice mismatch in heterostructures with a smaller number of layers.
the radiative characteristics are sensitive to the level of residual stresses in the active layer and can be improved by optimization of the stressed state of this layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an analysis of the relationship between radiative characteristics and the level of anisotropic stresses in the active layers of GaInAs/InP injection heterolasers.

the influence on the radiative properties of GaInAsp/InP lasers of anisotropic strain in the active layer that arises either as a result from external compression or as a result from the mismatch of the lattice parameters in heterojunction interfaces.
the development of a technique for optimizing the radiative characteristics and the production of laser diodes with improved parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the anisotropic deformation is a very important factor in determining the radiative characteristics, and that the sensitivity of these characteristics to the stressed state of a laser heterostructure should be taken into account in the development and optimization of laser devices.
, as a general rule, the lattices of the active layers of GaInAs(P)/InP laser diodes should be under compressive stress.
the radiative characteristics are very sensitive to anisotropic deformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiative characteristics can be improved by a proper selection of the lattice mismatch in the heterostructures.
it is necessary to optimize the stressed state of a laser diode to obtain the best radiative characteristics.
the radiative characteristics are determined not by the absolute values of the lattice periods in the active layer, but by the relative values of the mismatches in the heterostructures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to control the radiative characteristics by varying the degree of lattice mismatch and the temperature of the active layer of the laser diode.
the lasing wavelength and the radiative characteristics can be optimized by controlling the anisotropic deformation in the active layer.

it is necessary to control the stressed state of laser diodes and to optimize the lattice parameters of the layers in heterostructures in order to achieve a high level of their radiation characteristics and to ensure the stability of these characteristics.
